items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: I remember I met Bill Russell once when I was with Don Ewell.

ctx.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, I mentioned, yes, I mentioned that I had heard you with Baby Dodds, I'm quite certain about this, G-E-R-O-U-L-D. In a park on the edge of Lake Michigan at about 55th Street. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I think it was called Promontory Park or something of that sort. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And it was a field house or a band house or something of that sort out there in the park. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. On a weekend night, probably a Friday night, playing for a dance and some of the jazz enthusiasts at the school may have…

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I don't think so. I remember I met Bill Russell once when I was with Don Ewell. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Bill Russell came to town for something or other. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. I remember I met him once.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, Bill wasn't living here at that time then. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. No. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, alright. Then he wouldn't have run. Later on when he came into town he began to run some sessions.
